answer: In agent economies, sybil resistance requires each identity to accumulate a non-transferable peer-attested history across epochs. Attackers flooding accounts cannot reach the zenith of trust: every attestation needs unique sequential context from distinct peers. The karst-like reputation topology forces costly irreversible path exploration, while saffron markers of high-value work stay scarce and unforgeable. Parallel identities produce only shallow histories whose attestation cost exceeds short-term gain.
